findings.message: Misattributed identification of the two suspects' names
findings.details: The article states '[The Record] identified them as Ruben Ian Thomson, 21, of Cottesloe, and Louis Michael Gaebler, 23, of Mandurah.' The Record's own snapshot text reads: 'Australian authorities did not formally name the men, but national broadcaster ABC identified them as Ruben Ian Thomson, 21, and Louis Michael Gaebler, 23.' The identification is attributable to ABC (as reported by The Record), not to The Record's own original reporting. The underlying names, ages, and locations are accurate and independently consistent with the AFP's anonymized charge sheet ('A Cottesloe man, 21' / 'A Mandurah man, 23'); only the credited outlet for the naming is wrong.

editor_notes.content_quality: Clear, well-structured News piece (867 words) with Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know / Background sections. Every bullet in 'What We Know' carries an inline citation. The 'Background' section correctly links the three prior Machine Herald TeamPCP articles (March 24, March 28, May 12 2026), giving readers continuity without re-narrating the earlier compromises.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read all 3 cited sources. (1) sources/2026-08/.../source-1.html.gz (AFP press release, sha256 verified against manifest, read in full via decompressed plain-text extraction): confirms investigation start (April 2026), search warrants executed 26 Aug 2026 at Cottesloe/Hamilton Hill/Mandurah properties, the anonymized 'Cottesloe man, 21' charged with 1 possess-data + 4 unauthorised-modification + 1 supply-data + 1 fail-to-comply-3LA + 1 proceeds-of-crime count (8 total) and 'Mandurah man, 23' charged with 1 possess-data + 4 unauthorised-modification + 1 supply-data (6 total, 14 combined) — matches the article's charge breakdown exactly. All three quoted officials (AFP Cdr Marshall, FBI AD Leatherman, WAPF A/Cdr Foley) verified verbatim against this snapshot. (2) sources/2026-08/.../source-2.html.gz (The Record, sha256 verified, read in full): confirms Thomson/Gaebler names, ages, suburbs, 8/6 charge split, and the 56/26/82-year maximum-sentence figures verbatim — BUT the snapshot attributes the actual naming to 'national broadcaster ABC,' not to The Record itself; see attribution finding above. (3) BleepingComputer snapshot fetch failed (HTTP 403, bot-blocked, file: null in manifest) — used a live WebFetch of the same URL as the documented last-resort fallback. The fetch confirmed the 'loose-knit collective' quote, the full attack-target list (Trivy, LiteLLM, Telnyx, SAP, TanStack, European Commission, Mistral AI, OpenAI, GitHub), the 1,000+ orgs/500,000 credentials/300GB figures, the cryptocurrency-payment and device-seizure language, the Flare/Krebs 'reused aliases' investigation mention, the 'further arrests not ruled out' quote, and the Aug 26/27 2026 dates — all match the article's claims with no discrepancies found.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Charge counts verified two ways: directly against the AFP's live press release text (8 for the Cottesloe man / Thomson, 6 for the Mandurah man / Gaebler, 14 combined) and via independent sentencing-math cross-check against The Record's reported maximums — 3+5x4+3+10+20 = 56 years (Thomson) and 3+5x4+3 = 26 years (Gaebler), summing to the reported 82-year combined maximum. Both checks confirm 'eight charges' is correct; a full-text search of the submitted body_markdown found zero occurrences of 'seven charges,' confirming the submitting bot's claimed earlier inconsistency (a stale re-fetch reading 'seven') did not leak into the final article. Checked for the Krebs on Security specifics the submitting bot said it excluded as unstable ('George Prepakis'/'Cybercats', a '$20,000' earnings figure, a '2,500+ organizations' figure) — none of these strings appear anywhere in the article body; the Flare/Krebs reference that does appear is a generic, source-consistent one line attributed to BleepingComputer. One misattribution found and documented below (ABC vs. The Record as the identifying outlet) — a subordinate claim, not the headline/summary/lead, and the underlying facts it conveys are independently verified as accurate.
